item: W03/A02 recorded that the Magpie management surface was not located; this narrows it to a named, read-verified contract

gateway.name: magpie
gateway.probe: read-only GET requests against the loopback gateway that the launcher already discovers; no model call, no mutation

error.message: name the session: ?session=<id> or the X-Magpie-Session header

withoutASession.reading: the route is per session and is addressed either by the session query parameter or by the X-Magpie-Session header

withAnUnknownSession.reading: an unknown session is answered rather than refused: the current route is null and carries a sequence number, so a route is a versioned per-session value

notEstablished: whether a route is set by PUT or POST on the same path, and what a valid route payload looks like
what the sequence number does on a write

quotas.shape: an object list whose entries carry a provider, a kind (subscription or balance), optional plan and windows with used/remaining/reset values, a read time and a last-served time; the per-account values are deliberately not recorded here
quotas.reading: the gateway exposes its own quota view read-only; it is a management read, not a model call

notListedByOptions.reading: the gateway's own refusal message names the model routes only, so the management routes are a separate surface that discovery advertises and this refusal does not

notAttempted: setting a route for any session, including a synthetic one: it would change routing on a gateway the user is running
credential rotation: no rotation route is advertised, and any write against the live gateway is consequential
recordedWithoutValues: the quota response carries an account address, plan names and balances; none of those values are recorded in this file or anywhere in the evidence set
residual: the write half of route management and any credential-rotation surface remain unverified and require the user's go-ahead, because both change the running gateway
the read contract above was observed once against version 0.1.1109; it is a point observation, not a versioned guarantee
